newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMAN FIRST DIVISION WEEKEND MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMAN FIRST DIVISION WEEKEND MATCHES.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the German first division (league positions in parentheses.
Arminia Bielefeld (14) v Hamburg (13). This should be a tight affair with both teams needing points to get away from the relegation zone. Neither have won any of their last four games.

Bayer Leverkusen (3) v Karlsruhe (5). Leverkusen need three points to stay in touch with leading duo Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund. Coach Christoph Daum expected to name unchanged team despite defeat at Hansa Rostock last week. Karlsruhe will be a tough nut to crack with sights set on UEFA Cup place.

Duisburg (12) v Borussia Dortmund (2). Dortmund are struggling with injuries to defender Juergen Kohler, striker Karlheinz Riedle and wing back Stefan Reuter who will all miss the game. Libero Matthias Sammer also suspended and Brazilian defender Julio Cesar out for rest of season after knee operation. Duisburg cannot be underestimated having made a remarkable comeback from 2-0 down to thrash Cologne 5-2 last week.

Schalke (7) v Werder Bremen (9). Schalke have to keep their minds on making sure of a place in Europe next season despite their successful campaign in this season's UEFA Cup. Long-term injuries to strikers Martin Max and Dutchman Youri Mulder, who out for rest of season, have made the task even harder. Belgian forward Marc Wilmots is doubtful because of a shoulder problem.

VfB Stuttgart (4) v Hansa Rostock (16). Stuttgart must win games like this against struggling teams if they are serious about their challenge for the title. Stuttgart hope to have Dutch libero Frank Verlaat back in their ranks although he may have to play with strapping on injured left ankle.

Borussia Moenchengladbach (11) v Freiburg (18). Moenchengladbach have lifted their form in the second half of the season but are still too close to the relegation zone to feel completely safe. Their midfielder Stephan Passlack is suspended. Bottom club Freiburg look doomed to second division football next season.

St. Pauli (17) v 1860 Munich (6). Both teams involved in tight battles. St. Pauli want to avoid the drop, 1860 are in the running for a place in Europe next season. 1860 should be at full strength so Hamburg team will have a game on their hands.

Bayern Munich (1) v Cologne (10). Bayern looked impressive last weekend but the club is far from settled with rumours that coach Giovanni Trapattoni is wanted by Roma. German international midfielder Thomas Strunz set to return. Cologne need to get their minds focused after calamitous 5-2 defeat by Duisburg last Friday.

Bochum (8) v Fortuna Duesseldorf (15). Promoted Bochum still in with a shout for place in Europe next season but it is going to be hard. This is a match for picking up points since Duesseldorf have poor record of scoring away from home.
